bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Old gold exchange strategy aligns with government import reduction goals, creating a structural moat and ESG narrative; Inventory gains from customs duty hikes will flow through P&L over next 2 quarters, smoothing earnings; Sennes brand reached EBITDA profitability faster than expected (Year 2).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Equity raising history: "Raised INR 800 Mn equity from SAIF Partners India IV Limited (now Elevation Capital)" in 2015, "Raised INR 750 Mn equity from OIJIF II" in 2022, listing on NSE & BSE in 2023, and a QIP of Rs. 459 crore together with a 1:2 share split; both PE funds "Saif Partners and OIJIF II, monetized their investment".
- Vision 2030 return targets: ROE from 25.6% (FY26) to "20%+" and ROCE from 22.5% (FY26) to "20%+", with the CFO adding "a sharp focus on Return on Capital Employed (RoCE)".
- Stated financial priorities are margin and cash conversion rather than distribution: "Constantly Sharpen Profitability and Cash Flows" and "Generate robust Free Cash Flow for future expansion & working Capital need"; the CFO's focus list is "margin stabilization, improving inventory days, balancing finance cost through right mix of GML and optimizing subsidiary performance".
- The audited consolidated balance sheet shows Total Equity of Rs 25,136.8 Mn as at Mar-26 (Rs 19,702.9 Mn Mar-25, Rs 13,655.4 Mn Mar-24) against inventories of Rs 52,960.9 Mn, working capital borrowings of Rs 15,690.5 Mn and Gold Metal Loan of Rs 7,762.1 Mn.
- Franchising is framed as a return-on-equity device: "Franchisee store leads to higher ROE for Senco", with franchisee showrooms contributing "~33% of revenue" (proportion to revenue from operations excluding franchisee fees and discount allowed). The deck makes no mention of dividends or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- 87+ year heritage brand built on craftsmanship, integrity and customer-centricity, with a family lineage running from 1938 in Dhaka to a fourth-generation entrepreneur as MD & CEO
- Retail scale and density: 201 showrooms across 18 States and 1 UT plus Dubai, with stated market leadership in eastern India by number of stores
- Asset-light franchise model (79 FOFO and 6 FOCO stores) allowing expansion into new regions with optimal capital allocation alongside 102 owned stores
- Design catalogue depth: 218K gold jewellery designs and 122K diamond jewellery designs, with new designs released every month
- In-house manufacturing arm (SGAPL) plus a network of 277-plus master karigars, giving control over craftsmanship and quality
- Old gold exchange programme accounted for 44% of total FY26 sales, sustaining footfall and affordability at elevated gold prices
- Phy-gital / omni-channel reach: MySenco app (1.02 lakh downloads), DigiGold, DigiSilver, Sencoverse and Magic Mirror alongside physical showrooms
- Customer jewellery purchase schemes approved by the Registrar of Companies, with over 1,00,000 customers enrolled in the new 'Swarna Saubhagya' scheme and an average upsell of 10% at redemption, providing customer-led cash inflows
- Credit rating upgraded to CARE A+ during the year
- Quality and trust controls: gold purity and diamond carat testing, testing of old gold in front of customers, 100% hallmarking, multi-stage QC backed by lifelong buy-back
- Diversification optionality through Sennes (lab-grown diamonds, leather accessories, fragrances) and the Dubai subsidiary
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Margin risk - profitability heavily reliant on the gold jewellery segment — The Company states that profitability and margins are heavily reliant on the gold jewellery segment, so any supply disruption during gold procurement or adverse movement in market prices is a material financial risk. Gold jewellery accounted for ~85% of total revenue in FY26. Mitigation is product diversification into diamond, polki and platinum, and new verticals in leather accessories and lab-grown diamonds.
- Macroeconomic risk to discretionary consumer spending — Geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, elevated inflation, global monetary tightening and a broader slowdown threaten to limit discretionary spending, a direct risk to growth of the gems and jewellery industry. Mitigation cited is a strong domestic core, retail and e-commerce expansion, portfolio innovation and a broader geographic footprint so no single territory's cycle dominates.
- Competition risk from organised and unorganised players — The sector is characterised by intense competition from both organised and unorganised participants; failure to consistently deliver high-aesthetic, premium-quality products at competitive price points would directly threaten market share, revenue stability and long-term growth. Mitigation is brand equity, design portfolio depth, product innovation and brand amplification.
- Data security and privacy / data-protection compliance — The Company flags that data privacy infringement would materially affect the business and any breach could lead to non-compliance with data privacy law. Mitigation is cloud-based storage, software upgrades and continuous system hardening in line with new data privacy laws; ITGC audits are conducted by the internal auditors to mitigate cyber fraud and error risk.
- GHG emissions and energy management (BRSR material issue, classified a risk) — Purchased electricity in jewellery manufacturing and retail outlets raises Scope 2 emissions, and transportation and supply-chain activity raises Scope 3; the Company notes lab-grown diamonds are carbon intensive and will affect Scope 3 emissions in the long term. Stated financial implication is negative - it increases operational cost. Mitigation is energy-efficient lighting and air-conditioning, electricity monitoring, and evaluation of low-carbon transport and renewable energy.
- Water stewardship (BRSR material issue, classified a risk) — Water usage in offices and manufacturing is identified as a significant risk given potential water scarcity from climate-related water stress; stated financial implication is negative. Mitigation is low-flow fixtures, monitoring of water use and rainwater harvesting at selected locations.
- Single-activity and geographic concentration — BRSR Section A reports 100% of turnover from one main activity - manufacturing and retailing of jewellery with lifestyle and fashion accessories - across 18 States and 1 Union Territory, with exports contributing only 5% of total turnover and international presence limited to a single country. Earnings are therefore concentrated in one product category and one domestic market.
- Workforce attrition among permanent employees — BRSR turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 27.00% in FY 2025-26 from 24.20% in FY 2024-25 and 19.00% in FY 2023-24 (female attrition 32.00% in FY26), a structural retention pressure in a showroom-led, service-intensive retail model; permanent worker turnover by contrast is 1.00%.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Senco Gold Limited is one of India's leading jewellery retailers, backed by over eight decades of trusted family legacy", with a "Comprehensive product portfolio across gold, diamond, silver, platinum, and gemstone jewellery for every customer segment" and "Senco Gold & Diamonds" anchoring a multi-brand portfolio.
- Strategy slide frames the moat as "East stronghold, national footprint" — "Deepen the 87-year East India leadership in brand trust and density, using it to fund and de-risk expansion into non-East and Tier III/IV geographies"; West Bengal alone accounts for 109 of the 209 showrooms (47 own, 62 franchisee).
- Fourth-generation promoter family business: founded by Shri Maran Chand Sen in Tanti bazar, Dhaka in 1938, moved to Kolkata after Partition; Shri Shaankar Sen (Founder Chairman) joined in 1979 and grew it to over 100 showrooms; Shri Suvankar Sen (MD & CEO) joined in 2007 and listed the company on NSE and BSE in July 2023.
- Brand credentials cited include "2nd most trusted brand award by TRA Research in 2025", "MCX Best Hedger Award", "Entry into the Deloitte list of top 100 global Luxury brands", "Franchisor of the Year Award 2025" and "Great Place to Work Certificate 2025"; ICRA rating shown as "A+ (Stable)".
- Scale markers on the Business Highlights slide: 18 States & UTs, 133 Towns & Cities, 87+ years of legacy, 3.24 Mn+ loyal customers, 300k+ designs, 3,324+ team strength and 66% footfall conversion.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Hedging policy] A detailed gold-price risk framework: daily rate fixing of old gold, trading jewellery and GML "for the equivalent amount of gold sold ... ensures that there is no cash loss or business losses"; sales hedging at 90%-110% daily/weekly and inventory hedging at "~50% of gold inventory value as per board policy"; instruments are unfixed GML (~10% to ~40% of gold inventory, which "acts as a hedging instrument") and MCX Futures & Options sell positions (~10% to ~40%).
- [Hedge accounting] "Senco's hedge accounting is aligned with Ind AS 109 (IFRS 9)"; effective-hedge impact is "adjusted to inventory valuation through WACC method, thus impacting Gross Margin" while ineffective-hedge impact goes to other income/expenses. "Since Senco does not apply Cash Flow Hedge accounting, any reference to OCI or deferred recognition of hedge ineffectiveness is not applicable".
- [Customs duty] Management describes a customs-duty rise "from 6% to 15%" that caused demand contraction, and separately says "Indian gold prices are post-custom duty increase impact of 9%" with "The benefit of the custom duty rise ... likely to accrue over Q3, net of the impact of price fall due to the hedging level"; a footnote separately flags "one time adverse impact of custom duty reduction in FY25 which had been adjusted to Inventory and Gross Margin".
- [Labour code] "We have also considered full impact of Labour code in Q1 after detailed evaluation."
- [Subsidiary performance] "Business losses at SFL and SGJTL also affected consolidated profitability, while SGAPL continued to report profit" — SFL "is still in the growth phase and incurred losses" while the Dubai entity SGJTL "incurred losses due to extraordinary market situation in gulf based on gulf war and Hormuz imbroglio".
- [Regulatory environment] Sector regulation cited as mandatory hallmarking with HUID marking (mandatory from 2021, HUID mandatory from 2023), "Mandatory Hallmarking for 9 Carat Gold from July 2025", mandatory PAN for transactions over Rs 2,00,000, and Anti Money Laundering applicability with "CBIC designated as a regulator for the jewellery industry".
- [Industry sizing — deck contradicts itself] The strategy slide states "India's jewellery TAM: $90 Bn (FY25) → $130 Bn (FY30E), organised share rising 40% → 50%", while the industry section is titled "India's Gems and Jewellery Market likely to Scale to TAM of $ 162 Billion" and carries the figures 162, 106 and 115 (USD Bn) against FY25/FY26/FY30E. Both readings are recorded; they are not reconciled in the deck.
- [Market structure] India is described as "The 2nd Largest Jewellery Consuming Nation" at 26% of global consumption versus China 28%, "the 2nd largest gold market in the world", with 70% share of gold jewellery out of total gold demand, rural India at 60% of demand versus urban 40%, and gold jewellery falling from 84% (FY24) to 83% (FY29E) of the Indian market while studded rises 12% → 13%. West Bengal and Maharashtra each hold 17% of BIS-registered hallmarked gold jewellery retailers.
- [Technology stack] Eight-element digital framework listed as ERP driven organization, ISO Certification, Modern Digital Platforms, Centralized Network Management System, AI-Driven Customer Service, Data Driven Decision Making, 360° CRM platform and AI-Driven Martech, supporting an omnichannel "Phygital" hub-and-spoke fulfilment model.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company manufactures and retails jewellery made from gold, diamond, platinum, silver and other precious and semi-precious stones under the 'Senco Gold & Diamonds' brand, and retails lifestyle products - lab-grown diamond jewellery, premium leather accessories and fine fragrances - through its wholly owned subsidiary Sennes Fashion Limited. Distribution combines 102 Company-Owned (COCO) showrooms, 85 franchise-operated showrooms (79 FOFO and 6 FOCO), 12 Sennes lifestyle stores and 2 Dubai showrooms with digital touchpoints such as the MySenco app, DigiGold, DigiSilver and Sencoverse. Its customer base spans value-driven mass buyers to aspirational and premium segments across metros and tier-2, tier-3 and tier-4-and-below towns, with particularly strong traction among wedding shoppers and younger, design-conscious consumers; in-house manufacturing through Senco Gold Artisanship Pvt. Ltd. caters to about 7-8% of total sales.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Calibrated showroom expansion weighted towards franchise showrooms, in line with an explicitly asset-light strategy, after adding 26 showrooms net in FY26 to reach 201
- Premiumisation of the product portfolio through the studded and diamond range, which the CFO credits with catalysing the growth journey
- Broaden the entry-price and everyday-wear range through lightweight and lower-caratage jewellery across 22K, 18K, 14K and 9K, including the FY26 launch of 9-karat jewellery
- Deepen the 'Phy-gital' omni-channel model across online, offline and B2B channels through DigiGold, Magic Mirror and Sencoverse, with the old gold exchange programme as a key affordability enabler
- Diversify beyond gold through Sennes (lab-grown diamonds, premium leather accessories and fragrances), with management expecting lab-grown diamonds to become a dominant part of the Indian market within five years
- Improve inventory productivity under a 'SMART' framework - Strategic Stocking, Merchandise Monitoring, Assortment Optimisation, Replenishment Excellence and Technology-Driven Inventory
- Optimise borrowing cost by increasing the proportion of Gold Metal Loans in the borrowing mix, after the GML share fell from 67% to 33% in FY26
- Strengthen subsidiary performance (SGAPL, SGJTL, SFL) and the performance of showrooms in newer geographies
- Geographic diversification from the eastern-India base into a pan-India footprint while retaining market leadership in the east; Bengal and East India remain the stated engine for future growth
- Ethical sourcing and brand equity reinforcement, cited via the IAGES accreditation, alongside prudent hedging and disciplined inventory management
- Technology and AI deployment across the enterprise - 'Shape of You' personalisation, AI-powered customer engagement bots, location performance intelligence and AI-driven auto stock shuffling
- Unified HR policies across subsidiaries, leadership development (RAPID programme) and franchise HR standardisation via the Zing platform across 25+ franchisee locations
- This bundle carries no statement of dividend, reinvestment or balance-sheet philosophy. The only capital-allocation item present is the 32nd AGM agenda, which asks members to confirm the interim dividend already paid and to declare a final dividend for the year ended March 31, 2026; the Dividend Distribution Policy that governs it sits in the Board's Report, which was not routed to this domain.
- Energy: use of energy-efficient lighting and air-conditioning, monitoring of electricity consumption to reduce wastage, and active evaluation of low-carbon transport and renewable energy sources - stated as the mitigation for the GHG/energy material issue. No quantified emission or renewable-energy target is disclosed in this bundle.
- Water: conservation through low-flow fixtures, monitoring of water use to reduce wastage, and rainwater harvesting implemented at selected locations. No quantified water target is disclosed in this bundle.
- Responsible sourcing (identified as an opportunity, not a risk): materials sourced from environmentally and socially responsible suppliers, use of recycled gold to conserve foreign exchange and reduce the environmental and social impacts of mining, with the supplier base for ethical and responsible sourcing being increased through third-party certifications and audits.
- Governance: Board-level oversight on critical matters supported by regular training and robust audit and review mechanisms, identified as an ethical-governance opportunity; a Risk Management Committee constituted per statutory requirement performs risk assessment and minimisation, with the Board periodically reviewing the framework and a Risk Management Policy published on the website.
- Human rights / workplace: Whistle-Blower and Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) policies with designated committees; two POSH cases were filed during FY 2025-26 and zero remained pending at year end. Employee sentiment is tracked through 'Amber', an AI-enabled employee feedback platform.
- Diversity: 3 of 7 Board members are women (42.86%), 0 of 3 Key Management Personnel are women, and 1 of 7 Senior Management Personnel is a woman (14.29%); 18 differently-abled employees and 2 differently-abled workers are employed, and the Company reports four employees from the LGBTQ community.
- Stakeholder grievance redressal: documented mechanisms and published weblinks for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners; 2,375 customer complaints were filed in FY 2025-26 with 25 pending at year end (2,879 filed and 26 pending in FY 2024-25), and 2 shareholder complaints filed with none pending.
- CSR: applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013; a Board-level CSR Committee oversees the CSR framework and recommends the annual action plan under a published CSR Policy.
- Value chain partners: karigars, vendors and hallmarking centres are routed through their respective merchandisers for grievance resolution; no awareness programmes for value chain partners were conducted during the year (the BRSR leadership-indicator table is filled with dashes).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion at Senco is retail-footprint led rather than plant led. During FY26 the Company launched 26 showrooms (net addition of 26, after closing 2 COCO stores to improve capital efficiency), taking the network to 201 showrooms comprising 102 Company-Owned (COCO) stores, 85 franchise-operated stores (79 FOFO and 6 FOCO), 12 Sennes lifestyle stores and 2 international showrooms in Dubai operated through Senco Global Jewellery Trading LLC. Presence was extended into Rajasthan and Maharashtra through franchise models, with new geographies including Bikaner, Nagpur and Etawah, alongside a continued focus on Bengal and East India. Six of the additions were COCO stores, and the MD&A attributes part of the increase in borrowings to funding those 6 new COCO stores together with an inventory build-up of Rs 19,968 million ahead of the festive season and the West Bengal assembly elections; total borrowings rose from Rs 17,678.90 million in FY25 to Rs 23,452.60 million in FY26. Manufacturing capacity is provided by a dedicated in-house facility under Senco Gold Artisanship Pvt. Ltd., where local karigars handcraft designs; this facility caters to about 7-8% of total sales, and no installed capacity in physical units is disclosed. Investments in subsidiaries increased by Rs 100.00 million to Rs 414.84 million, entirely on account of capital infusions into Sennes Fashion Limited, and management states that the subsidiaries - especially SFL and SGJTL - will require sustained funding for future growth. The Company also began operating 20 Melorra franchise stores during the year, on which business support service expenses of Rs 200.2 million were incurred against nil in the previous year. Inventory days stand at ~183 days against a management target of 160-170 days, which the Company plans to close through AI-driven forecasting and smarter inter-store stock reallocation in FY27. Forward expansion intent, as stated in the outlook, is calibrated showroom expansion with an elevated roll-out of franchise showrooms in line with an asset-light strategy; no showroom-count target or rupee capex plan for FY27 is given in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Elevated and volatile gold prices are expected to persist amid global uncertainties; domestic gold prices rose ~79% YoY in FY26 to a peak of Rs 1,69,403 per 10 grams, expanding sales value even as physical gold volumes moderated by ~6%
- Recent changes in the customs duty structure on gold imports may influence demand in the short term
- Structural demand drivers described as firmly intact: jewellery's cultural, emotional and investment value, weddings and festivals, rising disposable incomes and a young demographic
- India's wedding industry is estimated at over Rs 10 lakh crore, with jewellery accounting for 25-35% of total wedding spend
- The Indian jewellery market is valued at ~US$ 90 billion and is expected to scale to US$ 130 billion by FY30, with the organised:unorganised split at 40:60 and the organised share expected to keep gaining
- Formalisation tailwind from mandatory hallmarking, GST compliance and anti-money-laundering norms shifting share to organised, branded players - described as a multi-year structural tailwind
- Elevated prices are expected to sustain the mix shift towards lightweight, lower-caratage, silver and studded jewellery
- Old gold exchange remains a key affordability enabler - 44% of total FY26 sales and ~50% of Q4 revenue
- Same Store Sales Growth of ~24% for FY26 (~35% in Q4) evidences the existing-showroom contribution to growth alongside new stores
- Margin levers cited: premiumisation and favourable product mix (reported gross margin 13.5% to 19.8%; adjusted gross margin 16.2%), against which management flags that excluding one-time gold-price gains the underlying EBITDA margin is ~8.5%
- Working capital intensity is structural: inventory rose 61% on gold prices, new showrooms and festive build-up, taking blended inventory holding to 186 days and leaving operating cash flow negative at Rs 7,893 million
- Financing cost driver: the GML share of borrowings fell from 67% to 33% because of margin-call-related liquidity pressure in volatile Q3/Q4, lifting the blended borrowing cost by 100 bps to 6.9%
- Emerging categories - lab-grown diamond alternatives and 9K/14K lightweight gold - are opening new product and consumer categories
- Management cautions on the evolving competitive landscape, elevated gold prices and global geopolitical uncertainties

risks.note: The Company states that profitability and margins are heavily reliant on the gold jewellery segment, so any supply disruption during gold procurement or adverse movement in market prices is a material financial risk. Gold jewellery accounted for ~85% of total revenue in FY26. Mitigation is product diversification into diamond, polki and platinum, and new verticals in leather accessories and lab-grown diamonds.
risks.risk: Margin risk - profitability heavily reliant on the gold jewellery segment

risks.note: Geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, elevated inflation, global monetary tightening and a broader slowdown threaten to limit discretionary spending, a direct risk to growth of the gems and jewellery industry. Mitigation cited is a strong domestic core, retail and e-commerce expansion, portfolio innovation and a broader geographic footprint so no single territory's cycle dominates.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic risk to discretionary consumer spending

risks.note: The sector is characterised by intense competition from both organised and unorganised participants; failure to consistently deliver high-aesthetic, premium-quality products at competitive price points would directly threaten market share, revenue stability and long-term growth. Mitigation is brand equity, design portfolio depth, product innovation and brand amplification.
risks.risk: Competition risk from organised and unorganised players

risks.note: The Company flags that data privacy infringement would materially affect the business and any breach could lead to non-compliance with data privacy law. Mitigation is cloud-based storage, software upgrades and continuous system hardening in line with new data privacy laws; ITGC audits are conducted by the internal auditors to mitigate cyber fraud and error risk.
risks.risk: Data security and privacy / data-protection compliance

risks.note: Purchased electricity in jewellery manufacturing and retail outlets raises Scope 2 emissions, and transportation and supply-chain activity raises Scope 3; the Company notes lab-grown diamonds are carbon intensive and will affect Scope 3 emissions in the long term. Stated financial implication is negative - it increases operational cost. Mitigation is energy-efficient lighting and air-conditioning, electricity monitoring, and evaluation of low-carbon transport and renewable energy.
risks.risk: GHG emissions and energy management (BRSR material issue, classified a risk)

risks.note: Water usage in offices and manufacturing is identified as a significant risk given potential water scarcity from climate-related water stress; stated financial implication is negative. Mitigation is low-flow fixtures, monitoring of water use and rainwater harvesting at selected locations.
risks.risk: Water stewardship (BRSR material issue, classified a risk)

risks.note: BRSR Section A reports 100% of turnover from one main activity - manufacturing and retailing of jewellery with lifestyle and fashion accessories - across 18 States and 1 Union Territory, with exports contributing only 5% of total turnover and international presence limited to a single country. Earnings are therefore concentrated in one product category and one domestic market.

BRSR turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 27.00% in FY 2025-26 from 24.20% in FY 2024-25 and 19.00% in FY 2023-24 (female attrition 32.00% in FY26), a structural retention pressure in a showroom-led, service-intensive retail model; permanent worker turnover by contrast is 1.00%.
